Note that plugging in $x=0$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{x}^{2}+3x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[{e}^{2x}-1]^{′}}{[{x}^{2}+3x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{2{e}^{2x}}{2x+3} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{2(0)}}{2(0)+3} \\  & =\frac{2(1)}{0+3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
